description: A marine fish with a streamlined body and greatly enlarged pectoral fins that allow it to glide above the water surface. It usually has a dark bluish upper body and a silvery underside. Members of this genus can leap from the water and glide considerable distances.
habitat: Warm tropical and subtropical marine waters; mainly found in surface and near-surface open-water environments.
diet: Mainly zooplankton, small crustaceans and other planktonic organisms.
conservation_status: Depends on the species. Exocoetus volitans, one species in this genus, is classified as Least Concern (LC) by the IUCN.
notes: Flying fish do not actually fly; they glide by leaping out of the water and using their enlarged pectoral fins as aerodynamic surfaces. They are important mid-level organisms in tropical marine food webs and are preyed upon by larger fish and seabirds.
sources: FishBase; Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS); peer-reviewed research on Exocoetus.

description: A slender, elongated marine fish belonging to the barracuda family Sphyraenidae. It has a streamlined, cylindrical body, a long pointed head, a large horizontal mouth and strong, sharp teeth. The upper surface is generally greenish while the underside is silvery. It can grow up to about 55 cm in total length.
habitat: Found mainly in tropical marine and brackish waters. It commonly inhabits bays, estuaries, seagrass beds and rocky reefs, and may occur at depths of approximately 5–200 m. It is often found in groups in coastal habitats.
diet: It is a carnivorous predator that feeds mainly on smaller fishes. Studies from the Indian coast have also recorded crustaceans and cephalopods as part of its diet. Fish were the dominant prey in a study conducted along the Karnataka coast.
conservation_status: Least Concern (LC) according to the IUCN Red List assessment dated 14 August 2023.
notes: The species is commercially important and is caught in coastal fisheries. It is a mainly daytime-active predator and plays a role in controlling populations of smaller fish and other marine organisms. Research from India's west coast has also documented its feeding habits and reproductive biology.
sources: FishBase; ICAR–Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute; Indian Journal of Fisheries.

common_name: Horse Mackerel / Finletted Mackerel Scad / Torpedo Scad
description: A fast-swimming marine fish with an elongated, slightly compressed body. It is bluish-grey or greenish on the upper side and becomes silvery toward the belly. It has a prominent black spot near the upper rear edge of the gill cover, strong scutes along the lateral line, and several small finlets behind the dorsal and anal fins. It can reach about 80 cm in length.
habitat: Mainly found in tropical and subtropical marine waters of the Indo-West Pacific, from East Africa through the Indian Ocean to Japan and Australia. Adults are generally pelagic and occur in schools, usually at depths of about 20–100 m. They may also occur in coastal and brackish waters.
diet: Primarily carnivorous, feeding mainly on smaller fishes. Its diet may also include other small marine organisms.
conservation_status: Least Concern (LC) according to the IUCN Red List assessment.
notes: Megalaspis cordyla belongs to the family Carangidae, which includes jacks, pompanos and scads. It is an important commercial fish and is commonly marketed fresh for human consumption. Its streamlined body and powerful tail make it well adapted for active swimming in open water.
sources: FishBase; Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS); Australian Museum; World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS).
